I am weighing whether to build hotels on the orange properties. Three hotels would cost $300 and leave me with $58. The rent increase is only $200 per property, so the investment seems marginal. I also need to consider p3's $705 and pink monopoly as a potential risk.

Standard Monopoly rent tables show p3's pink properties would cost $100 per house. p4's yellow monopoly costs $50 per house. p2's red properties cost $18 per house. These figures help assess whether p3 can build enough houses to threaten my orange holdings.

I am reviewing the rent tables for p3's pink, yellow, green, and dark blue monopolies. I also need to determine whether p3 will move before my next turn.

p3 will act after p2, p3, and p4. They paid $35 rent to p4 on Park Place last turn, so they can build houses before rolling. If they spend $700 on pink properties, two houses each would cost $150 in rent.

I am mapping the board positions from Community Chest. Rolling a 2 lands on Income Tax for $200. Rolling a 3 lands on Baltic Avenue, which p3 currently owns with no houses and only $4 in rent. Rolling a 4 lands on Reading Railroad, where p4 holds two railroads and would charge $50.

Oriental Avenue is just $6 rent because p4 does not own the full light blue set. Rolling 5 from Community Chest lands on Oriental, rolling 7 lands on Vermont, and rolling 8 lands on Connecticut.

Rolls 10 and 12 from Community Chest would land on p3's pink properties. If p3 builds seven houses, Virginia with three houses costs $500. I only have $358, so I would need to sell houses at half price.

Selling three houses would raise my cash to $508, enough to cover a $500 pink rent. Building hotels now would leave only $58, and if I hit Virginia with three houses I would have to sell hotels back to houses and then sell houses at half price. That is too tight and would sacrifice the hotel advantage. The strategic value of four houses versus a hotel is now being weighed.

Upgrading to hotels would return twelve houses to the bank. The house shortage is a weapon. p3 could then build a full hotel row on pink and light blue.

p3 can afford seven houses because cash is the limit, not the bank's supply. p2 can buy one more house on red, but must build on Kentucky or Indiana first to even out his set. If I keep my houses, p3 still has enough to build seven, so the house shortage does not bind yet.

Hotels require four houses per property, so p3 cannot build them immediately even if I return the houses to the bank. The classic strategy is to keep four houses and create a housing shortage that blocks opponents from building. p2 can afford one more house, but p4 has no cash for any upgrades.

Building hotels would raise rent by only $200 per hit. I would be left with just $58 cash, which is too little to survive a decent orange rent without selling houses or hotels. p2 would still go bankrupt on a hit whether I have four houses or hotels, because $750 already exceeds his liquidity. p4 has no cash for any orange rent. The upgrade does not improve my position.

If p3 does not build on pink before rolling, a $750 orange rent would bankrupt them and hand me their light blue and pink monopolies. They will almost certainly spend their cash on pink first.

p3 cannot reach orange from Park Place in a single roll. The board positions confirm that rolling 2 through 12 from space 37 lands on Luxury Tax and Boardwalk, not the orange properties at spaces 16 through 19. p2 is also too far behind to catch up this turn.

p3 cannot afford four houses on the pink properties. The shortage does not constrain their current build this turn.

I am reconsidering the housing shortage. If I build hotels, p3 would need twelve houses to reach four on each pink property before they could upgrade to hotels. The bank currently holds only thirteen houses, so p3 cannot afford that many. Hotels do not require extra houses from the bank if a player already has four; they simply pay and return their existing houses. This means p3 cannot build hotels immediately even if I return the houses to the bank.

The housing shortage is mild. p3 could eventually reach four houses and hotel if they had enough cash, but they do not have it now. Cash safety is the stronger reason to avoid hotels. I am now weighing the threats before my next income.
